passages.text: For the choirmaster. According to Gittith. Of Asaph.
passages.sermon: This psalm is for the choirmaster.\r\nAsaph wrote this psalm.\r\nThe music should be played according to Gittith.

passages.text: Sing for joy to God our strength; make a joyful noise to the God of Jacob.
passages.sermon:
This psalm is for the choirmaster.
Asaph wrote it.
God is our strength.
Sing for joy to God.
The God of Jacob is our God.
Make a joyful noise to Him.
passages.original: לַמְנַצֵּ֬חַ׀ עַֽל־ הַגִּתִּ֬ית לְאָסָֽף׃ הַ֭רְנִינוּ לֵאלֹהִ֣ים עוּזֵּ֑נוּ הָ֝רִ֗יעוּ לֵאלֹהֵ֥י יַעֲקֹֽב׃

passages.text: Lift up a song, strike the tambourine, play the sweet-sounding harp and lyre.
passages.sermon:
Asaph wrote this psalm for the choirmaster.
He called the people to worship God.
Lift up a song.
Strike the tambourine.
Play the harp.
Play the lyre.
The harp and lyre sound sweet.
passages.original: שְֽׂאוּ־ זִ֭מְרָה וּתְנוּ־ תֹ֑ף כִּנּ֖וֹר נָעִ֣ים עִם־ נָֽבֶל׃

passages.text: Sound the ram’s horn at the New Moon, and at the full moon on the day of our Feast.
passages.sermon:
God commanded Israel to celebrate special days.
God is the God of Jacob.
Sound the ram’s horn at the New Moon.
Sound the ram’s horn at the full moon.
Do this on the day of our Feast.
passages.original: תִּקְע֣וּ בַחֹ֣דֶשׁ שׁוֹפָ֑ר בַּ֝כֵּ֗סֶה לְי֣וֹם חַגֵּֽנוּ׃

passages.text: For this is a statute for Israel, an ordinance of the God of Jacob.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel a law.
God made this law a rule for His people.
God is the God of Jacob.
God commanded this law as an ordinance for Israel.
passages.original: כִּ֤י חֹ֣ק לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל ה֑וּא מִ֝שְׁפָּ֗ט לֵאלֹהֵ֥י יַעֲקֹֽב׃

passages.text: He ordained it as a testimony for Joseph when he went out over the land of Egypt, where I heard an unfamiliar language: “I relieved his shoulder of the burden; his hands were freed from the basket.
passages.sermon:
God gave a command as a testimony for Joseph.
Joseph left the land of Egypt.
In Egypt, I heard a language I did not know.
I removed the heavy load from Joseph’s shoulder.
I set his hands free from carrying the basket.
passages.original: עֵ֤דוּת׀ בִּֽיה֘וֹסֵ֤ף שָׂמ֗וֹ בְּ֭צֵאתוֹ עַל־ אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם שְׂפַ֖ת לֹא־ יָדַ֣עְתִּי אֶשְׁמָֽע׃ הֲסִיר֣וֹתִי מִסֵּ֣בֶל שִׁכְמ֑וֹ כַּ֝פָּ֗יו מִדּ֥וּד תַּעֲבֹֽרְנָה׃

passages.text: You called out in distress, and I rescued you; I answered you from the cloud of thunder; I tested you at the waters of Meribah. Selah Hear, O My people, and I will warn you: O Israel, if only you would listen to Me!
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Israel.
God says, “You called out when you were in trouble.
I rescued you.
I answered you from the secret place of thunder.
I tested you at the waters of Meribah.
Selah.
Listen, My people.
I will warn you.
Israel, if only you would listen to Me.”
passages.original: בַּצָּרָ֥ה קָרָ֗אתָ וָאֲחַ֫לְּצֶ֥ךָּ אֶ֭עֶנְךָ בְּסֵ֣תֶר רַ֑עַם אֶבְחָֽנְךָ֨ עַל־ מֵ֖י מְרִיבָ֣ה סֶֽלָה׃ שְׁמַ֣ע עַ֭מִּי וְאָעִ֣ידָה בָּ֑ךְ יִ֝שְׂרָאֵ֗ל אִם־ תִּֽשְׁמַֽע־ לִֽי׃

passages.text: There must be no strange god among you, nor shall you bow to a foreign god.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people Israel.
God commands them.
You must not have a strange god among you.
You must not bow down to a foreign god.
passages.original: לֹֽא־ יִהְיֶ֣ה בְ֭ךָ אֵ֣ל זָ֑ר וְלֹ֥א תִ֝שְׁתַּחֲוֶ֗ה לְאֵ֣ל נֵכָֽר׃

passages.text: I am the LORD your God, who brought you up out of Egypt. Open wide your mouth, and I will fill it.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people Israel.
God says, “I am the LORD.
I am your God.
I brought you out of Egypt.
Open your mouth wide.
I will fill your mouth.”
passages.original: אָנֹכִ֨י׀ יְה֘וָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ הַֽ֭מַּעַלְךָ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם הַרְחֶב־ פִּ֝֗יךָ וַאֲמַלְאֵֽהוּ׃

passages.text: But My people would not listen to Me, and Israel would not obey Me.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to His people.
God’s people are called Israel.
God’s people did not listen to God’s voice.
Israel did not want to obey God.
passages.original: וְלֹא־ שָׁמַ֣ע עַמִּ֣י לְקוֹלִ֑י וְ֝יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לֹא־ אָ֥בָה לִֽי׃

passages.text: So I gave them up to their stubborn hearts to follow their own devices.
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD.
God brought Israel out of Egypt.
God’s people did not listen to Him.
God let them go their own way.
God allowed them to follow their stubborn hearts.
God let them act according to their own plans.

passages.text: If only My people would listen to Me, if Israel would follow My ways, how soon I would subdue their enemies and turn My hand against their foes!
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people, Israel.
God wants His people to listen to Him.
God wants Israel to follow His ways.
If Israel listens to God, God will act quickly.
God will defeat Israel’s enemies.
God will turn His hand against Israel’s foes.
passages.original: ל֗וּ עַ֭מִּי שֹׁמֵ֣עַֽ לִ֑י יִ֝שְׂרָאֵ֗ל בִּדְרָכַ֥י יְהַלֵּֽכוּ׃ כִּ֭מְעַט אוֹיְבֵיהֶ֣ם אַכְנִ֑יעַ וְעַ֥ל צָ֝רֵיהֶ֗ם אָשִׁ֥יב יָדִֽי׃

passages.text: Those who hate the LORD would feign obedience, and their doom would last forever.
passages.sermon: Those who hate the LORD pretend to obey Him.\r\nTheir punishment lasts forever.
passages.original: מְשַׂנְאֵ֣י יְ֭הוָה יְכַֽחֲשׁוּ־ ל֑וֹ וִיהִ֖י עִתָּ֣ם לְעוֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: But I would feed you the finest wheat; with honey from the rock I would satisfy you.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God promises to care for them.
God says, “I would feed you the best wheat.
I would give you honey from the rock.
I would satisfy you with good things.”
passages.original: וַֽ֭יַּאֲכִילֵהוּ מֵחֵ֣לֶב חִטָּ֑ה וּ֝מִצּ֗וּר דְּבַ֣שׁ אַשְׂבִּיעֶֽךָ׃
